## 5. The matching construction

### 5.1 The naive first moment

Suppose we choose $S \subseteq [n]$ uniformly at random among sets of size $m = \lceil \delta n\rceil$.
For a fixed set $W \subseteq [n]$ with $|W| = L$,
$$\Pr[W \subseteq S] \;=\; \frac{\binom{n-L}{m-L}}{\binom{n}{m}} \;\le\; \left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^{L}.$$
Hence, if $\mathcal{W}$ is a family of "witnesses" (sets that any forbidden configuration
must contain) with $|\mathcal{W}| \cdot (m/n)^{L} < 1$, some $m$-element $S \subseteq [n]$
contains no member of $\mathcal{W}$, and therefore no forbidden configuration.

For sumsets of two $K$-term arithmetic progressions
$\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,K) + \mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,K)$, the family is parameterised by
$(a + b, d_1, d_2)$ — only the sum $a+b$ matters — giving at most $n^3$ witnesses; each
sumset contains the "L-shaped" witness of $2K - 1$ points. The condition
$n^3 (m/n)^{2K-1} < 1$ holds once
$$K \;\ge\; \Big(\tfrac{3}{2}+\varepsilon\Big)\frac{\log n}{\log(1/\delta)},$$
giving the intermediate constant $3/2$.

### 5.2 Weighted first moment

The improvement to $1$ comes from two observations.

**(i) A variable-size first-moment principle.** Let $\{W_i\}_{i \in I}$ be a finite family
of subsets of $[n]$ with $|W_i| \ge L_i \ge 1$. If
$$\sum_{i \in I} \left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^{L_i} \;<\; 1,$$
then some $m$-element $S \subseteq [n]$ contains no $W_i$. (Same proof as above, without
assuming the $L_i$ equal.)

**(ii) Blocks beat L-shapes.** Write $d_1 = g e_1$, $d_2 = g e_2$ with
$\gcd(e_1,e_2) = 1$ and set $Q = \max(e_1,e_2)$. Then
$$\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,K) + \mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,K)
= \{a + b + g(i e_1 + j e_2) : 0 \le i,j < K\}.$$
Because $e_1$ and $e_2$ are coprime, the map $(i,j)\mapsto i e_1 + j e_2$ is injective on
$0 \le i < K$, $0 \le j < \min(Q, K)$; hence the sumset contains a **block witness** of
$$K \cdot \min(Q, K)$$
distinct points. The L-shaped bound $2K-1$ is the truth only when $Q = 1$, i.e. $d_1 = d_2$.

**(iii) The parameter count does not grow with $Q$.** For fixed $Q$, the triples
$(t, g, e_1, e_2)$ with $t < n$, $\max(e_1,e_2) = Q$ and $g e_i < n$ number at most
$2n^2$ — the constraint $\max(e_1,e_2) = Q$ pins one of the two cofactors, and $g$ ranges
over at most $n/Q$ values. Combining with the witness sizes
$$L(K,Q) \;=\; \max\big(2K-1,\; K\min(Q,K)\big)$$
(the L-shape is always available, the block is available when $Q \ge 2$), the weighted first
moment is bounded by
$$\sum_{Q \ge 1} 2n^{2}\,x^{\,L(K,Q)}, \qquad x = m/n \le \delta + 1/n .$$
The terms decay geometrically in $Q$ (each increment of $Q$ below $K$ adds $K$ to the
exponent), so once $2x^{K}\le 1$ the sum is at most twice its first term, $4n^{2}x^{2K-1}$.
The binding constraint is therefore the *equal-difference* case $Q = 1$, where only $n^2$
parameters occur and the witness has $2K - 1$ points:
$$4n^{2}x^{2K-1} < 1 \iff (2K-1)\log(1/x) > 2\log n + \log 4,$$
i.e. $K > (1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ once the rounding loss $x \le \delta + 1/n$
and the constant factors are absorbed into $\varepsilon$. Compared with the naive bound,
what has been saved is exactly the third factor of $n$: the parameter $d_1/d_2$ ratio is no
longer free, because when it is nontrivial the witness is a fat block rather than an L.

> **Theorem 5.3 (Counting form).** Let $m \le n$, $m \ge 1$, $K \ge 2$, and set $x = m/n$.
> If $2x^{K} \le 1$ and the weighted sum above is $< 1$, then there is $S \subseteq [n]$
> with $|S| = m$ containing no sumset $\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,K') + \mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,K')$ with
> $d_1,d_2 > 0$ and $K' \ge K$.

> **Theorem 5.4 (Avoidance at constant $1$).** For every $0 < \delta < 1$ and
> $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $n_0$ such that for all $n \ge n_0$ there exists
> $S \subseteq [n]$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ and
> $$\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,K) + \mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,K) \not\subseteq S$$
> for all $a, b$, all $d_1, d_2 > 0$ and all
> $K \ge (1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.

*Proof sketch.* Set $m = \lceil \delta n\rceil$, so $x = m/n \le \delta + 1/n$. Choose
$\theta = \varepsilon/(2(1+\varepsilon))$; for $n$ large enough, $1/(\delta n) \le \theta\log(1/\delta)$,
which converts $\log(1/x) \ge (1-\theta)\log(1/\delta)$. Two further largeness conditions,
$\log(1/\delta) + \log 16 \le \varepsilon \log n$ and $4\log(1/\delta) \le \log n$, make the
constants in the geometric series harmless. Then Theorem 5.3 applies with
$K = \lceil (1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)\rceil$. $\square$

### 5.3 Progression-rich pairs and the min-form

The constructed set avoids far more than sumsets of progressions.

> **Theorem 5.5 (Progression-rich avoidance).** For every $0 < \delta < 1$ and
> $\varepsilon > 0$, for all large $n$ there is $S \subseteq [n]$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$
> such that: whenever $A$ and $B$ each contain an arithmetic progression of length
> $T \ge (1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ (with positive common difference), we have
> $A + B \not\subseteq S$.

*Proof.* If $\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,T) \subseteq A$ and $\mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,T)\subseteq B$ then
$\mathrm{AP}(a,d_1,T) + \mathrm{AP}(b,d_2,T) \subseteq A + B$, so containment of $A+B$ in
$S$ would contradict Theorem 5.4. $\square$

In particular, taking $A, B$ to be progressions of possibly *different* lengths $K_1, K_2$
and applying the theorem with $T = \min(K_1,K_2)$ gives the statement in the form in which
the problem is usually posed: no sumset of two progressions with
$\min\{|A|,|B|\}\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ lies inside $S$.

> **Theorem 5.6 (Two-sided threshold).** Fix $0 < \delta < 1$, $\varepsilon > 0$, and
> $c>0$ with $c\log(1/\delta)<1$. For all sufficiently large $n$ *both* of the following
> hold:
> 1. every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ contains a sumset $A+B$ with
>    $|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$;
> 2. some $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ contains no sumset $A+B$ with $A,B$ both
>    containing a progression of length $\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.
>
> Since $c$ may be taken arbitrarily close to $1/\log(1/\delta)$, the threshold is
> $(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$: the extremal constant equals $1$.

*Proof.* Intersect the two eventual statements of Theorems 4.4 and 5.5. $\square$

The asymmetry deserves emphasis: the existence half is unconditional on the *shape* of
$A, B$, while the avoidance half applies to pairs that are progression-rich. Section 9
discusses this gap.

## 6. Affine cubes: the multi-fold companion

### 6.1 Iterating the engine on its own output

The greedy step of Lemma 3.2 can be applied with $U$ equal to the *current survivor set*
rather than to $S$, and the shift can be recorded as a new cube generator. Write
$$\mathcal{C}(a_1,\dots,a_j) = \{0,a_1\}+\cdots+\{0,a_j\}$$
for the cube of shifts built so far. The invariant maintained is: there is a set $U_j$ with
$u + x \in S$ for every $u \in U_j$ and every $x \in \mathcal{C}(a_1,\dots,a_j)$, together
with the counting bound
$$|S|^{2^{j}} \;\le\; (2|D|)^{2^{j}-1}\,|U_j| .$$
Each new generator squares the exponent, because the new survivor set must be compatible
with the entire old cube *and* its translate: $|U_{j+1}| \gtrsim |U_j|^2/|D|$.

> **Theorem 6.1 (Abstract cube criterion).** Let $D$ absorb all differences of $S$ with
> $|D| \ge 2$. If
> $$2\,(2|D|)^{2^{j}-1} \;\le\; |S|^{2^{j}} \qquad \text{for every } j \le d,$$
> then there are $u \in S$ and nonzero $a_1,\dots,a_d$ with
> $\mathcal{C}(u;a_1,\dots,a_d)\subseteq S$.

A convenient reduction: if $|S| \le 2|D|$ (always true in our applications) the condition
at the top scale $j = d$ implies it at every $j \le d$, since the ratio $|S|/(2|D|) \le 1$
only decreases under higher powers.

> **Theorem 6.2 (Cubes in finite abelian groups).** If $|G| \ge 2$ and
> $2(2|G|)^{2^d-1} \le |S|^{2^d}$, then $S \subseteq G$ contains an affine cube of dimension
> $d$ with nonzero generators. The same holds in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ with $|G| = N$.

> **Theorem 6.3 (Cubes in intervals).** Let $S \subseteq [0,n)$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ and
> $n \ge 1$, $\delta > 0$. If
> $$\left(\frac{4}{\delta}\right)^{2^{d}} \;\le\; 2n,$$
> equivalently $d \le \log_2\!\big(\log(2n)/\log(4/\delta)\big)$, then $S$ contains an
> affine cube of dimension $d$ with all generators nonzero (possibly negative).

*Proof sketch.* Use $D = (-n,n)$, so $|D| = 2n-1$ and $2|D| \le 4n$; the abstract condition
$2(4n)^{2^d-1} \le |S|^{2^d}$ follows from $|S| \ge \delta n$ once
$(4/\delta)^{2^d} \le 2n$, by writing $(\delta n)^{2^d} = (\delta/4)^{2^d}(4n)^{2^d}$. $\square$

The doubly logarithmic dimension is intrinsic: each step squares the density loss, so after
$d$ steps the density is $\delta^{2^d}$, and the process halts when $\delta^{2^d} n \approx 1$,
i.e. at $2^d \approx \log n/\log(1/\delta)$ — exactly where the two-fold argument halts at
$k \approx \log n /\log(1/\delta)$. This is a quantitative form of Szemerédi's cube lemma,
obtained here from the same averaging step as the two-fold bound.

### 6.2 Properness

A cube produced by Theorem 6.3 can be degenerate: if $a_1 = a_2$ it collapses to a
three-term progression, and a dense set certainly contains those. To force all $2^d$ subset
sums to be distinct, run the same iteration but forbid each new shift from lying in the
difference set
$$\mathcal{C}(a_1,\dots,a_j) - \mathcal{C}(a_1,\dots,a_j),$$
which has at most $4^{j}$ elements. A shift outside it is automatically nonzero and doubles
the cardinality of the cube, so properness is maintained.

> **Lemma 6.4.** If $a \notin \mathcal{C}(l) - \mathcal{C}(l)$ then
> $|\mathcal{C}(a, l)| = 2|\mathcal{C}(l)|$.

> **Theorem 6.5 (Proper cubes in intervals).** Let $S \subseteq [0,n)$, $|S| \ge \delta n$,
> $0 < \delta \le 1$, $n \ge 1$. If
> $$\left(\frac{4}{\delta}\right)^{2^{d}}\cdot 4^{d} \;\le\; 2n,$$
> then $S$ contains a *proper* affine cube of dimension $d$: nonzero generators
> $a_1,\dots,a_d$ and a base $u \in S$ with all $2^d$ points
> $u + \sum_{i\in I}a_i$ distinct and in $S$.

The only change from Theorem 6.3 is the factor $4^{d}$, which shifts the admissible range
of $d$ by $O(\log d)$ in the exponent $2^d$ — nothing on the scale
$2^d \approx \log n/\log(1/\delta)$.

### 6.3 The matching first-moment bound

A $d$-dimensional cube in $[n]$ is determined by its base and $d$ generators, hence there
are at most $n^{d+1}$ of them; a proper one forces $2^d$ points of $S$.

> **Theorem 6.6 (Cube-free dense sets).** For every $0 < \delta < 1$ and $\varepsilon > 0$,
> for all sufficiently large $n$ and *every* dimension $d$ with
> $$(1+\varepsilon)\,(d+1)\log n \;\le\; 2^{d}\log(1/\delta),$$
> there exists $S \subseteq [n]$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ containing no proper
> $d$-dimensional affine cube with positive generators.

*Proof sketch.* With $m = \lceil \delta n\rceil$ the first-moment condition is
$n^{d+1}m^{L} < n^{L}$ with $L = 2^d$; this is exactly
$(d+1)\log n < 2^d \log(n/m)$, and $\log(n/m) \ge \log(1/(\delta + 1/n))$, which exceeds
$\log(1/\delta)/(1+\varepsilon)$ for large $n$. Note that the exponent $d+1$ must be allowed
to grow with $n$, so the analytic step is carried out for unbounded exponents. $\square$

> **Theorem 6.7 (One set for all dimensions).** For every $0 < \delta < 1$ and
> $\varepsilon>0$, for all large $n$ and every $d_0$ with
> $$(1+\varepsilon)(d_0+1)\log(4n) \;\le\; 2^{d_0}\log(1/\delta),$$
> there exists a single $S \subseteq [n]$ with $|S| \ge \delta n$ containing no proper
> affine cube of *any* dimension $d \ge d_0$.

*Proof sketch.* Apply the variable-size first-moment principle of §5.2(i) to the union over
all $d \ge d_0$ of the cube families, with $L_d = 2^d$ and $|I_d| = n^{d+1}$. Two facts make
the total sum finite and small: a proper $d$-cube in $[n]$ has $2^d \le n$ points, so only
$d \le n$ occur; and the ratio $(d+1)/2^{d}$ is nonincreasing, so the threshold hypothesis
need only be checked at $d = d_0$. The resulting series is dominated by
$\sum_{j\ge1}4^{-j} \le 1/3$. $\square$

> **Theorem 6.8 (Disjointness of the two ranges).** For every $0<\delta<1$ and
> $\varepsilon>0$, for all sufficiently large $n$ no dimension $d$ satisfies both the
> existence condition $(4/\delta)^{2^d}4^{d}\le 2n$ of Theorem 6.5 and the avoidance
> condition $(1+\varepsilon)(d+1)\log n \le 2^{d}\log(1/\delta)$ of Theorem 6.6.

*Proof sketch.* The existence condition gives $2^{d}\log(4/\delta) \le \log 2 + \log n$,
hence $2^{d}\log(1/\delta) \le \log 2 + \log n$; the avoidance condition gives
$2^{d}\log(1/\delta) \ge (1+\varepsilon)(d+1)\log n \ge (1+\varepsilon)\log n$. These
conflict once $\varepsilon \log n > \log 2$. $\square$

So the critical dimension for proper cubes lies between the two thresholds, and both are of
the shape $2^{d} \asymp \log n/\log(1/\delta)$ — up to the additive $\log_2(d+1)$ which is
$O(\log\log\log n)$ in the exponent scale.

---

## 7. Effective instances

Because Theorem 3.4 and Theorem 6.1 are exact inequalities between integers, they can be
instantiated at concrete numbers with no asymptotic slack. Four samples:

| Statement | Numerical check |
|---|---|
| Every $S \subseteq [0,2^{20})$ with $\lvert S\rvert \ge 2^{19}$ contains $A+B$, $\lvert A\rvert=\lvert B\rvert=7$ | $7\cdot(2^{21})^{7} \le 2^{19}(2^{19}-7)^{7}$ |
| Every $S \subseteq [0,2^{22})$ with $\lvert S\rvert \ge 2^{19}$ contains $A+B$, $\lvert A\rvert=\lvert B\rvert=4$ | $4\cdot(2^{23})^{4} \le 2^{19}(2^{19}-4)^{4}$ |
| Every $S\subseteq[0,4096)$ with $\lvert S\rvert\ge2048$ contains $u,u+a,u+b,u+a+b$ ($a,b\neq0$) | $2\,(4\cdot4096)^{3} = 2^{43} \le 2048^{4}=2^{44}$ |
| Every $S\subseteq[0,32768)$ with $\lvert S\rvert\ge16384$ contains a *proper* $2$-cube | $2\cdot4^{2}(4\cdot32768)^{3} = 2^{56} \le 16384^{4} = 2^{56}$ |

The last line is an exact equality — the criterion is tight at that instance.

---

## 8. Algorithmic content

The existence half of the theory is constructive, and the construction is a short
polynomial-time algorithm.

**Greedy sumset extraction.** Input: $S \subseteq [0,n)$, target $k$.
1. Set $U \leftarrow S$, $A \leftarrow \emptyset$.
2. Repeat $k$ times: over all shifts $a \in D \setminus A$, compute
   $f(a) = |\{u \in U : u + a \in S\}|$; choose $a^*$ maximising $f$; set
   $A \leftarrow A \cup \{a^*\}$, $U \leftarrow \{u \in U : u + a^* \in S\}$.
3. If $|U| \ge k$, output $A$ and any $k$-subset $B \subseteq U$.

Each round costs $O(|D|\cdot|U|)$ membership tests, so the whole run is $O(k\,n\,|S|)$ in
the worst case with a bitset representation reducing this to $O(k n^2/64)$ word operations;
in practice $U$ shrinks geometrically and the cost is dominated by the first round.
Theorem 3.4 guarantees success whenever $k|D|^k \le |S|(|S|-k)^k$; in experiments the
algorithm typically succeeds well beyond that guarantee, since the greedy choice
consistently beats the average.

**Greedy cube extraction.** Identical, except that $U$ is replaced by the current survivor
set and the update is $U \leftarrow U \cap (U - a^*)$, doubling the cube dimension count by
one each round; to force properness, restrict $a^*$ to lie outside
$\mathcal{C}-\mathcal{C}$ for the cube built so far.

**Threshold computation.** Both criteria are monotone in $k$ (resp. $d$), so the maximal
guaranteed $k$ is found by a single scan or a binary search on the inequality; the
arithmetic must be done in exact integers (or in logarithms) because the quantities involved
have thousands of digits already for $n = 2^{20}$.

---

## 9. Discussion, limitations, open problems

**What is exactly determined.** For pairs $(A,B)$ in which both factors are
progression-rich, the extremal threshold in $[n]$ is
$(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$, and the constant $1$ is best possible on both sides. In
finite abelian groups the existence side holds with the same constant with respect to
$\log |G|$, with a cleaner proof (no window loss).

**The asymmetry.** The existence theorem produces *arbitrary* $A, B$; the avoidance
theorem defeats only *progression-rich* $A,B$. Closing this gap — i.e. constructing, for
$K \ge (1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$, a $\delta$-dense set containing no sumset
$A+B$ with $|A| = |B| = K$ and $A, B$ arbitrary — is the main open problem left here. The
obstruction is a counting one: the family of all pairs of $K$-element sets is far too large
for a union bound, and any successful construction must exploit the structure that a
$K \times K$ additive grid imposes on its own factor sets (Freiman-type rigidity), rather
than enumerating them.

**Sharpness of the greedy engine.** The counting criterion $k|D|^k\le|S|(|S|-k)^k$ is tight
in shape but not in constants: the greedy step only claims the maximum beats the average,
and the "already used shifts" are charged at the maximal rate $|U|$ each. Refined accounting
(e.g. second-moment control of the shift-count distribution) might improve the lower-order
terms, though not the leading constant, which is already matched.

**Cubes.** For proper affine cubes the existence and avoidance ranges of $d$ are disjoint
and both located at $2^{d}\asymp\log n/\log(1/\delta)$, but they differ by the additive
$\log_2(d+1)+O(1)$ in $d$. Determining the critical dimension to within an additive
constant — that is, deciding whether the truth sits at
$2^{d}\approx \log n/\log(1/\delta)$ or at $2^{d}\approx (d+1)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ — is a
natural next target. The gap is exactly the "$d+1$ parameters" of the union bound versus the
"one parameter per dimension" of the greedy construction.

**Beyond two factors.** The cube results are the $d$-fold companion for two-element
factors. The general question — the largest $r$-fold sumset $A_1+\cdots+A_r$ with all
$|A_i| = k$ forced inside a $\delta$-dense set — interpolates between the two regimes and
is governed by the same squaring phenomenon: with $r$ factors of size $k$ the density loss
per factor is $\delta^{k}$, so one expects $rk\approx\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ for the total
"volume" $\sum \log|A_i|$ of the configuration. Making this precise, with matching
constants, would unify Sections 3–5 with Section 6.

**Groups versus intervals.** The interval bound needed the short-window trick to shed a
factor $2$; in a group no trick is needed. This suggests that the interval problem's
lower-order terms carry genuine boundary information, and it would be interesting to
determine the second-order term in $[n]$ — whether it is $-\Theta(\log\log n)$ or $O(1)$.

---

## 10. Summary of the main statements

1. **Averaging identity.** For $U \subseteq S$ and $D \supseteq S - S$:
   $\sum_{a\in D}\#\{u\in U : u+a\in S\} = |U||S|$.
2. **Counting criterion.** $k|D|^{k}\le|S|(|S|-k)^{k}$ implies $A+B\subseteq S$ with
   $|A|=|B|=k$, $A \subseteq D$.
3. **Groups.** For $c\log(1/\delta)<1$ and $|G|$ large, every $\delta$-dense $S\subseteq G$
   contains $A+B$ with $|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log|G|\rfloor$.
4. **Intervals.** The same with $\log n$, for every $\delta$-dense $S\subseteq[n]$.
5. **Avoidance.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and large $n$, some $\delta$-dense
   $S\subseteq[n]$ contains no $A+B$ with $A,B$ both containing a progression of length
   $\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.
6. **Threshold.** The extremal constant for progression-rich sumsets is exactly $1$:
   the threshold is $(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.
7. **Cubes.** $(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}\le 2n$ forces a $d$-dimensional affine cube;
   $(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}4^{d}\le2n$ forces a proper one;

   even for all $d\ge d_0$ at once.

\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}

Given a set $S$ of integers, when must $S$ contain a \emph{product structure} --- a sumset
$A+B$ with both factors large? A sumset is the additive analogue of a combinatorial
rectangle: a $|A|\times|B|$ grid of sums, determined by $|A|+|B|$ parameters but imposing
$|A|\cdot|B|$ membership conditions. Containing a large sumset is therefore a strong
regularity property, and the extremal question --- how large a sumset is forced by density
alone? --- sits at the interface of the pigeonhole and probabilistic halves of additive
combinatorics.

Fix $0<\delta<1$, write $[n]=\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, and call $S\subseteq[n]$
\emph{$\delta$-dense} if $|S|\ge\delta n$. Define $C(\delta)$ as the infimum of constants
$c$ such that for all large $n$ some $\delta$-dense $S\subseteq[n]$ contains no sumset
$A+B\subseteq S$ with $\min\{|A|,|B|\}\ge c\log n/\log(1/\delta)$. Both the shape
$\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ and the finiteness of $C(\delta)$ follow from an iterated pigeonhole
and a union bound respectively; the content of this paper is the exact leading constant.

\subsection{Results}

Throughout $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
\item \textbf{Existence, exact constant.} For $c\log(1/\delta)<1$ and all large $n$, every
$\delta$-dense $S\subseteq[n]$ contains $A+B$ with $|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp-interval}).
\item \textbf{Avoidance, exact constant.} For every $\varepsilon>0$ and large $n$, some
$\delta$-dense $S\subseteq[n]$ contains no sumset $A+B$ in which both factors contain a
progression of length $\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:rich}).
\item \textbf{Threshold.} Consequently the threshold for progression-rich sumsets is
$(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:threshold}).
\item \textbf{Groups.} In any finite abelian group the existence bound holds with no window
loss (Theorem~\ref{thm:group}).
\item \textbf{Cubes.} Existence of $d$-dimensional affine cubes for
$(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}\le2n$, proper cubes for $(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}4^{d}\le2n$, and matching
avoidance above the first-moment threshold (Section~\ref{sec:cubes}).
\item \textbf{Effective instances.} E.g.\ every $S\subseteq[0,2^{20})$ with $|S|\ge2^{19}$
contains a sumset with $|A|=|B|=7$ (Section~\ref{sec:instances}).
\end{itemize}

\section{Notation}

$[n]=\{0,\dots,n-1\}$; $A+B=\{a+b\}$, $A-B=\{a-b\}$. For $a,d,K\in\N$,
$\AP(a,d,K)=\{a,a+d,\dots,a+(K-1)d\}$; if $d>0$ it has $K$ elements. A finite set $A$ is
\emph{$T$-progression-rich} if $\AP(a,d,T)\subseteq A$ for some $a$ and some $d>0$.

\begin{definition}[Affine cube]
For $u,a_1,\dots,a_d$ in an abelian group,
\[
\Cube(u;a_1,\dots,a_d)=u+\{0,a_1\}+\cdots+\{0,a_d\}
=\Big\{u+\sum_{i\in I}a_i : I\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}\Big\}.
\]
It has at most $2^{d}$ elements and is \emph{proper} when it has exactly $2^{d}$.
\end{definition}

\section{The greedy shift engine}

\subsection{The averaging identity}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging identity]\label{lem:avg}
Let $S,D,U$ be finite subsets of an abelian group with $U\subseteq S$, and suppose
$s-u\in D$ for all $u,s\in S$. Then
\[
\sum_{a\in D}\#\{u\in U : u+a\in S\}=|U|\cdot|S|.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Exchange the order of summation:
$\sum_{a\in D}\#\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}=\sum_{u\in U}\#\{a\in D:u+a\in S\}$. Fix
$u\in U\subseteq S$: the map $a\mapsto u+a$ is injective and sends
$\{a\in D:u+a\in S\}$ into $S$, and every $s\in S$ arises from $a=s-u\in D$. Hence the inner
count is $|S|$ for each $u$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{One greedy step}

\begin{lemma}[Good shift]\label{lem:step}
With $S,D,U$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:avg}, let $F$ be a set of already used shifts with
$|F|<|D|$. Then there exists $a\in D\setminus F$ with
\[
|U|\,|S|\;\le\;|D|\cdot\#\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}+|F|\,|U|,
\]
equivalently $\#\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}\ge|U|(|S|-|F|)/|D|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write $f(a)=\#\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}$ and split the sum of Lemma~\ref{lem:avg} over $D\cap F$
and $D\setminus F$. Each term of the first part is at most $|U|$, contributing at most
$|F||U|$; the second is at most $|D|\max_{a\in D\setminus F}f(a)$, and $D\setminus F\ne
\emptyset$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Iteration and the counting criterion}

\begin{proposition}[Greedy iteration]\label{prop:iter}
Let $D$ absorb all differences of $S$ and $k\le\min(|S|,|D|)$. For every $j\le k$ there are
$A\subseteq D$ with $|A|=j$ and $U\subseteq S$ with $u+a\in S$ for all $a\in A,u\in U$, and
\[
|S|\,(|S|-k)^{j}\;\le\;|U|\,|D|^{j}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Induction on $j$; for $j=0$ take $A=\emptyset$, $U=S$. For the step apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:step} with $F=A$ (so $|F|=j<k\le|D|$), giving a fresh shift $a$ and
$U'=\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}$. Since $(|S|-k)+j\le|S|$,
\[
|U|(|S|-k)+|A|\,|U|\le|U||S|\le|D||U'|+|A||U|,
\]
so $|U|(|S|-k)\le|D||U'|$; multiplying the inductive bound by $(|S|-k)$ gives the claim.
Compatibility holds for the new shift by construction and for old shifts since
$U'\subseteq U$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Counting criterion]\label{thm:criterion}
Let $D$ absorb all differences of the finite set $S$ in an abelian group, and let
$k\le\min(|S|,|D|)$ satisfy
\[
k\,|D|^{k}\;\le\;|S|\,(|S|-k)^{k}.
\]
Then there are $A\subseteq D$ and $B$ with $|A|=|B|=k$ and $A+B\subseteq S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $j=k$ in Proposition~\ref{prop:iter}: $k|D|^{k}\le|S|(|S|-k)^{k}\le|U||D|^{k}$, so
$k\le|U|$; choose $B\subseteq U$ with $|B|=k$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Instances of the window}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em]
\item \emph{Finite abelian group}: $D=G$, criterion $k|G|^{k}\le|S|(|S|-k)^{k}$; with
$|S|=\delta|G|$ this is $k(1/\delta)^{k}\lesssim\delta|G|$, i.e.\ $k\lesssim
\log|G|/\log(1/\delta)$: no loss.
\item \emph{Integer interval, naive window}: $S\subseteq[0,n)\subseteq\Z$, $D=(-n,n)$ of
size $2n-1$; criterion $k(2n)^{k}\le|S|(|S|-k)^{k}$, giving
$k\lesssim\log n/\log(2/\delta)$.
\item \emph{Natural numbers}: translate $A$ by its minimum and $B$ by its negative; the
sumset is unchanged and both factors become sets of nonnegative integers.
\end{itemize}

\section{From counting to density}

\begin{lemma}[Real-parameter criterion]\label{lem:real}
Let $D$ absorb all differences of $S$, let $k\le|D|\le M$, let $\sigma\le|S|$ and
$0<\epsilon<1$. If $k\le\epsilon\sigma$ and
$k\big(M/((1-\epsilon)\sigma)\big)^{k}\le\sigma$, then $S$ contains $A+B$ with
$|A|=|B|=k$, $A\subseteq D$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$k\le\epsilon\sigma$ gives $|S|-k\ge(1-\epsilon)\sigma$; substitute into
Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion}.
\end{proof}

The analytic engine is elementary: if $b>1$ and $c\log b<1$ then for every $\alpha>0$,
$\lfloor c\log N\rfloor\,b^{\lfloor c\log N\rfloor}\le\alpha N$ for all large $N$, since
$b^{c\log N}=N^{c\log b}=N^{1-\eta}$ with $\eta>0$.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp lower bound in finite abelian groups]\label{thm:group}
Fix $0<\delta<1$ and $c>0$ with $c\log(1/\delta)<1$. There is $N_0$ such that for every
finite abelian group $G$ with $|G|\ge N_0$ and every $S\subseteq G$ with $|S|\ge\delta|G|$
there exist $A,B$ with $|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log|G|\rfloor$ and $A+B\subseteq S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:real} with $D=G$, $M=|G|$, $\sigma=\delta|G|$, small fixed $\epsilon$
and $k=\lfloor c\log|G|\rfloor$: the hypothesis becomes
$k(1/((1-\epsilon)\delta))^{k}\le\delta|G|$, valid for large $|G|$ since
$c\log(1/((1-\epsilon)\delta))<1$ for $\epsilon$ small.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Intervals: removing the window loss}

The greedy iteration never needs $D$ to contain \emph{all} differences of $S$; it needs only
a uniform lower bound $\#\{a\in D:u+a\in S\}\ge m$ for $u$ in the starting set $U_0$. All of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:avg}--\ref{lem:step} and Proposition~\ref{prop:iter} hold in this one-sided
form (in a commutative monoid), with $|U||S|$ replaced by $m|U|$.

\begin{lemma}[Short window]\label{lem:window}
Let $S\subseteq[0,n)$, $1\le w\le n$, $D=[0,n-w+1)$. For every $u<w$,
$\#\{a\in D:u+a\in S\}\ge|S|-(w-1)$.
\end{lemma}

Partitioning $[0,n)$ into $\lceil n/w\rceil$ blocks of length $w$ and choosing, by
pigeonhole, a block $I$ with $|S\cap I|\ge|S|w/n$ supplies a starting set inside a window of
length $w$, at the cost of a constant factor. The shift window now has $\approx n$ elements
instead of $2n$.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp lower bound in $[n]$]\label{thm:sharp-interval}
Fix $0<\delta<1$ and $c>0$ with $c\log(1/\delta)<1$. For all sufficiently large $n$,
\emph{every} $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ contains a sumset $A+B$ with
$|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $t=1-c\log(1/\delta)>0$ and $r=e^{-t/(2c)}\in(0,1)$, so $c\log(1/(\delta r))<1$. Choose
the window length $w$ so that the pigeonhole loss and the additive loss $w-1$ degrade the
effective density from $\delta$ to at least $\delta r$. The one-sided criterion then applies
with $|D|\le n$, $m\ge\delta r n$ and $k=\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$, and the required inequality
holds for large $n$ by the analytic engine.
\end{proof}

\section{The matching construction}

\subsection{The naive first moment}

For $S\subseteq[n]$ uniform of size $m$ and fixed $W$ with $|W|=L$,
$\Pr[W\subseteq S]\le(m/n)^{L}$. Hence if a family $\mathcal W$ of witnesses satisfies
$|\mathcal W|(m/n)^{L}<1$, some $m$-element $S$ contains no member of $\mathcal W$. For
sumsets of two $K$-term progressions the parameters are $(a+b,d_1,d_2)$, at most $n^{3}$
choices, and each sumset contains an L-shaped witness of $2K-1$ points; the condition
$n^{3}(m/n)^{2K-1}<1$ yields the intermediate constant $3/2$.

\subsection{Weighted first moment}

\begin{lemma}[Variable-size first moment]\label{lem:weighted}
Let $\{W_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of subsets of $[n]$ with $|W_i|\ge L_i\ge1$. If
$\sum_{i\in I}(m/n)^{L_i}<1$, then some $m$-element $S\subseteq[n]$ contains no $W_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Block witness]\label{lem:block}
Write $d_1=ge_1$, $d_2=ge_2$ with $\gcd(e_1,e_2)=1$ and $Q=\max(e_1,e_2)$. Then
\[
\AP(a,d_1,K)+\AP(b,d_2,K)=\{a+b+g(ie_1+je_2): 0\le i,j<K\}
\]
contains $K\cdot\min(Q,K)$ distinct points, since $(i,j)\mapsto ie_1+je_2$ is injective for
$0\le i<K$, $0\le j<\min(Q,K)$.
\end{lemma}

For fixed $Q$ the number of admissible triples $(t,g,e_1,e_2)$ with $t<n$ and
$\max(e_1,e_2)=Q$ is at most $2n^{2}$, independently of $Q$. Writing
\[
L(K,Q)=\max\big(2K-1,\;K\min(Q,K)\big)
\]
for the number of points a sumset with ratio $Q$ is forced to contain (the L-shape is always
available, the block whenever $Q\ge2$), the weighted first moment is bounded by
\[
\sum_{Q\ge1}2n^{2}x^{\,L(K,Q)},\qquad x=m/n\le\delta+1/n .
\]
The terms decay geometrically in $Q$, so once $2x^{K}\le1$ the sum is at most twice its
first term, $4n^{2}x^{2K-1}$. The binding case is therefore $Q=1$ (equal common
differences), where only $n^{2}$ parameters occur and the witness has $2K-1$ points:
$4n^{2}x^{2K-1}<1$ is equivalent to $(2K-1)\log(1/x)>2\log n+\log4$, i.e.\
$K>(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$. Compared with the naive bound, what has been
saved is precisely the third factor of $n$: the ratio $d_1/d_2$ is no longer a free
parameter, because when it is nontrivial the witness is a fat block rather than an L.

\begin{theorem}[Avoidance at constant $1$]\label{thm:avoid}
For every $0<\delta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$ there
is $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ and
$\AP(a,d_1,K)+\AP(b,d_2,K)\not\subseteq S$ for all $a,b$, all $d_1,d_2>0$ and all
$K\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $m=\lceil\delta n\rceil$, so $x\le\delta+1/n$; with
$\theta=\varepsilon/(2(1+\varepsilon))$ and $n$ large, $1/(\delta n)\le\theta\log(1/\delta)$,
which converts the rounding loss into $\log(1/x)\ge(1-\theta)\log(1/\delta)$. Two further
largeness conditions, $\log(1/\delta)+\log16\le\varepsilon\log n$ and
$4\log(1/\delta)\le\log n$, absorb the constants of the geometric series. Now apply
Lemmas~\ref{lem:weighted} and~\ref{lem:block} with
$K=\lceil(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)\rceil$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Progression-rich avoidance]\label{thm:rich}
For every $0<\delta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, for all large $n$ there is $S\subseteq[n]$ with
$|S|\ge\delta n$ such that whenever $A$ and $B$ each contain an arithmetic progression of
length $T\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ with positive common difference, we have
$A+B\not\subseteq S$. In particular no sumset of two progressions with
$\min\{|A|,|B|\}\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ lies in $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $\AP(a,d_1,T)\subseteq A$ and $\AP(b,d_2,T)\subseteq B$ then the sumset of the two
progressions lies inside $A+B$, contradicting Theorem~\ref{thm:avoid}. The min-form follows
by applying this with $T=\min(K_1,K_2)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two-sided threshold]\label{thm:threshold}
Fix $0<\delta<1$, $\varepsilon>0$ and $c>0$ with $c\log(1/\delta)<1$. For all sufficiently
large $n$ both hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ contains $A+B$ with
$|A|=|B|=\lfloor c\log n\rfloor$;
\item some $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$ contains no $A+B$ with $A,B$ both
containing a progression of length $\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$.
\end{enumerate}
Since $c$ may be taken arbitrarily close to $1/\log(1/\delta)$, the threshold is
$(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$: the extremal constant equals $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Intersect the eventual statements of Theorems~\ref{thm:sharp-interval} and~\ref{thm:rich}.
\end{proof}

\section{Affine cubes}\label{sec:cubes}

Applying the greedy step with $U$ equal to the current survivor set (rather than $S$) and
recording each shift as a new cube generator maintains the invariant that
$u+x\in S$ for all $u\in U_j$ and all $x\in\Cube(a_1,\dots,a_j)$, together with
\[
|S|^{2^{j}}\;\le\;(2|D|)^{2^{j}-1}\,|U_j|,
\]
since $|U_{j+1}|\gtrsim|U_j|^{2}/|D|$: each generator squares the density loss.

\begin{theorem}[Abstract cube criterion]\label{thm:cube-abs}
Let $D$ absorb all differences of $S$, $|D|\ge2$. If $2(2|D|)^{2^{j}-1}\le|S|^{2^{j}}$ for
every $j\le d$, then there are $u\in S$ and nonzero $a_1,\dots,a_d$ with
$\Cube(u;a_1,\dots,a_d)\subseteq S$. If moreover $|S|\le2|D|$, the condition at $j=d$
implies it at all $j\le d$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cubes in intervals]\label{thm:cube-int}
Let $S\subseteq[0,n)$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$, $n\ge1$, $\delta>0$. If
$(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}\le2n$ --- equivalently $d\le\log_2(\log(2n)/\log(4/\delta))$ --- then
$S$ contains an affine cube of dimension $d$ with all generators nonzero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $D=(-n,n)$, so $2|D|\le4n$; the abstract condition $2(4n)^{2^{d}-1}\le|S|^{2^{d}}$
follows from $|S|\ge\delta n$ by writing $(\delta n)^{2^{d}}=(\delta/4)^{2^{d}}(4n)^{2^{d}}$.
\end{proof}

The doubly logarithmic dimension is intrinsic: after $d$ steps the density is
$\delta^{2^{d}}$, so the process halts at $2^{d}\approx\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ --- exactly
where the two-fold argument halts at $k\approx\log n/\log(1/\delta)$. This is a quantitative
form of the cube lemma of Szemer\'edi, here obtained from the same averaging step.

\begin{lemma}[Properness step]\label{lem:proper}
If $a\notin\Cube(a_1,\dots,a_j)-\Cube(a_1,\dots,a_j)$ then
$|\Cube(a,a_1,\dots,a_j)|=2|\Cube(a_1,\dots,a_j)|$.
\end{lemma}

Forbidding each new shift to lie in that difference set (of size at most $4^{j}$) keeps the
cube proper and its generators nonzero.

\begin{theorem}[Proper cubes in intervals]\label{thm:proper}
Let $S\subseteq[0,n)$ with $|S|\ge\delta n$, $0<\delta\le1$, $n\ge1$. If
$(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}\cdot4^{d}\le2n$, then $S$ contains a proper affine cube of dimension
$d$: nonzero $a_1,\dots,a_d$ and $u\in S$ with all $2^{d}$ points $u+\sum_{i\in I}a_i$
distinct and in $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cube-free dense sets]\label{thm:nocube}
For every $0<\delta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, for all large $n$ and every $d$ with
$(1+\varepsilon)(d+1)\log n\le2^{d}\log(1/\delta)$, there is $S\subseteq[n]$ with
$|S|\ge\delta n$ containing no proper $d$-dimensional affine cube with positive generators.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
With $m=\lceil\delta n\rceil$, the first-moment condition $n^{d+1}m^{L}<n^{L}$ with
$L=2^{d}$ reads $(d+1)\log n<2^{d}\log(n/m)$, and
$\log(n/m)\ge\log(1/(\delta+1/n))>\log(1/\delta)/(1+\varepsilon)$ for large $n$. The
exponent $d+1$ is allowed to grow with $n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One set for all dimensions]\label{thm:nocube-all}
For every $0<\delta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, for all large $n$ and every $d_0$ with
$(1+\varepsilon)(d_0+1)\log(4n)\le2^{d_0}\log(1/\delta)$, there is a single $S\subseteq[n]$
with $|S|\ge\delta n$ containing no proper affine cube of any dimension $d\ge d_0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:weighted} to the union over $d\ge d_0$ of the cube families, with
$L_d=2^{d}$ and $n^{d+1}$ parameters. A proper $d$-cube in $[n]$ has $2^{d}\le n$ points, so
only $d\le n$ occur; and $(d+1)/2^{d}$ is nonincreasing, so the hypothesis need only be
checked at $d=d_0$. The resulting series is dominated by $\sum_{j\ge1}4^{-j}\le1/3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Disjointness of the ranges]\label{thm:window}
For every $0<\delta<1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, for all large $n$ no dimension $d$ satisfies
both $(4/\delta)^{2^{d}}4^{d}\le2n$ and $(1+\varepsilon)(d+1)\log n\le2^{d}\log(1/\delta)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The first gives $2^{d}\log(1/\delta)\le2^{d}\log(4/\delta)\le\log2+\log n$; the second gives
$2^{d}\log(1/\delta)\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n$. These conflict once $\varepsilon\log n>\log2$.
\end{proof}

\section{Effective instances}\label{sec:instances}

Theorems~\ref{thm:criterion} and~\ref{thm:cube-abs} are exact integer inequalities, so they
instantiate with no asymptotic slack.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
Statement & Numerical check\\
\midrule
$S\subseteq[0,2^{20})$, $|S|\ge2^{19}$ $\Rightarrow$ $A+B\subseteq S$, $|A|=|B|=7$
 & $7\,(2^{21})^{7}\le2^{19}(2^{19}-7)^{7}$\\
$S\subseteq[0,2^{22})$, $|S|\ge2^{19}$ $\Rightarrow$ $A+B\subseteq S$, $|A|=|B|=4$
 & $4\,(2^{23})^{4}\le2^{19}(2^{19}-4)^{4}$\\
$S\subseteq[0,4096)$, $|S|\ge2048$ $\Rightarrow$ $u,u+a,u+b,u+a+b\in S$
 & $2\,(4\cdot4096)^{3}=2^{43}\le2048^{4}=2^{44}$\\
$S\subseteq[0,32768)$, $|S|\ge16384$ $\Rightarrow$ proper $2$-cube
 & $2\cdot4^{2}(4\cdot32768)^{3}=2^{56}\le16384^{4}=2^{56}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The last line is an exact equality: the criterion is tight at that instance.

\section{Algorithmic content}

The existence half is constructive.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Greedy sumset extraction.} Input $S\subseteq[0,n)$ and a target $k$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=2em]
\item $U\leftarrow S$, $A\leftarrow\emptyset$.
\item Repeat $k$ times: for $a\in D\setminus A$ compute $f(a)=|\{u\in U:u+a\in S\}|$; pick
$a^{*}$ maximising $f$; set $A\leftarrow A\cup\{a^{*}\}$, $U\leftarrow\{u\in U:u+a^{*}\in S\}$.
\item If $|U|\ge k$, output $A$ and any $k$-subset $B\subseteq U$.
\end{enumerate}
Each round costs $O(|D|\cdot|U|)$ membership tests; with a bitset representation the total
is $O(kn^{2}/64)$ word operations, and in practice $U$ shrinks geometrically.
Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} guarantees success whenever $k|D|^{k}\le|S|(|S|-k)^{k}$; in
experiments the algorithm succeeds well beyond the guarantee, since the greedy maximum
consistently beats the average.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Greedy cube extraction.} Identical, but the update is
$U\leftarrow U\cap(U-a^{*})$, adding one dimension per round; for properness restrict
$a^{*}$ to lie outside $\Cube-\Cube$ for the cube built so far.

\section{Discussion and open problems}

\paragraph{What is determined.} For pairs $(A,B)$ in which both factors are
progression-rich, the extremal threshold in $[n]$ is $(1+o(1))\log n/\log(1/\delta)$, with
the constant $1$ best possible on both sides. In finite abelian groups the existence side
holds with the same constant with respect to $\log|G|$ and a cleaner proof.

\paragraph{The asymmetry.} The existence theorem produces arbitrary $A,B$; the avoidance
theorem defeats only progression-rich $A,B$. Constructing a $\delta$-dense set containing no
sumset of two arbitrary $K$-element sets with $K\ge(1+\varepsilon)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ is
the main open problem left here: the family of all pairs of $K$-sets is far too large for a
union bound, and a successful construction must exploit the rigidity a $K\times K$ additive
grid imposes on its factor sets.

\paragraph{Cubes.} For proper cubes the existence and avoidance ranges of $d$ are disjoint
and both located at $2^{d}\asymp\log n/\log(1/\delta)$, but differ by the additive
$\log_2(d+1)+O(1)$ in $d$. Determining the critical dimension to within an additive constant
--- deciding between $2^{d}\approx\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ and
$2^{d}\approx(d+1)\log n/\log(1/\delta)$ --- is a natural next target.

\paragraph{Beyond two factors.} The general $r$-fold problem, with factors of size $k$,
interpolates between the two regimes and is governed by the same squaring phenomenon: one
expects the total ``volume'' $\sum_i\log|A_i|$ of the configuration to be
$\approx\log n/\log(1/\delta)$. Making this precise with matching constants would unify the
two halves of this paper.

\paragraph{Groups versus intervals.} The interval bound required the short-window trick to
shed a factor $2$, whereas no trick is needed in a group. This suggests the interval
problem's lower-order terms carry genuine boundary information; determining the second-order
term in $[n]$ --- $-\Theta(\log\log n)$ or $O(1)$ --- is open.

Dense sets and the sumsets they cannot escape
=============================================

Numerical companion to "The Exact Threshold for Sumsets in Dense Sets of Integers".

Everything here is exact integer arithmetic (Python ints are unbounded), so the
"certificates" printed below are genuine verifications of the counting criteria,
not floating-point approximations.

Contents
--------
1.  counting_criterion / max_guaranteed_k
        The exact criterion  k*|D|^k <= |S|*(|S|-k)^k  and the largest k it certifies.
2.  greedy_sumset
        The constructive greedy shift algorithm: given a concrete dense set S,
        it produces A, B with A + B subset of S.
3.  greedy_cube / is_proper_cube
        The same engine iterated on its own output, producing affine cubes
        u + {0,a_1} + ... + {0,a_d}.
4.  avoidance_threshold
        The first-moment (avoidance) threshold  (1+eps) log n / log(1/delta).
5.  Verification of the four effective instances stated in the paper.

Run:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from itertools import combinations
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The exact counting criterion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def counting_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Exact criterion of the greedy shift argument.

    Returns True iff  k * window**k <= s_card * (s_card - k)**k,
    where `window` is the size of the admissible shift domain D and `s_card` = |S|.

    Whenever this holds (and k <= min(|S|, |D|)), *every* set S of that size inside
    the corresponding ambient interval/group contains a sumset A + B with
    |A| = |B| = k and A drawn from the shift window.
    """
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return k * window**k <= s_card * (s_card - k) ** k


def _log_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Logarithmic screening version of `counting_criterion` (cheap for huge inputs)."""
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return math.log(k) + k * math.log(window) <= math.log(s_card) + k * math.log(s_card - k)


def max_guaranteed_k(window: int, s_card: int) -> int:
    """Largest k certified by `counting_criterion` (the criterion is monotone in k).

    A logarithmic screening pass locates the crossover cheaply even for astronomically
    large windows; the answer is then confirmed with exact integer arithmetic.
    """
    lo, hi = 0, min(window, s_card)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        if _log_criterion(mid, window, s_card):
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    # exact confirmation in a small neighbourhood of the float crossover
    k = lo
    while k > 0 and not counting_criterion(k, window, s_card):
        k -= 1
    while counting_criterion(k + 1, window, s_card):
        k += 1
    return k


def interval_guarantee(n: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Guaranteed sumset size for a delta-dense subset of [0, n), naive window D = (-n, n)."""
    return max_guaranteed_k(2 * n, math.ceil(delta * n))


def group_guarantee(order: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Guaranteed sumset size for a delta-dense subset of an abelian group of given order."""
    return max_guaranteed_k(order, math.ceil(delta * order))


def asymptotic_prediction(n: int, delta: float) -> float:
    """The theoretical value log n / log(1/delta)."""
    return math.log(n) / math.log(1.0 / delta)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Constructive greedy shift extraction of a sumset
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def greedy_sumset(
    S: Set[int], n: int, k: int
) -> Optional[Tuple[List[int], List[int]]]:
    """Greedy shift algorithm.

    Repeatedly pick the unused shift a in (-n, n) maximising |{u in U : u + a in S}|,
    and replace U by that surviving set.  After k rounds, if |U| >= k, the collected
    shifts A and any k-subset B of U satisfy A + B subset of S.

    Returns (A, B) or None if the greedy run does not reach size k.
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    A: List[int] = []
    used: Set[int] = set()
    for _ in range(k):
        best_a, best_survivors = None, None
        # candidate shifts: differences of S are the only ones that can help
        candidates = {s - u for s in S for u in U} - used if len(U) < 200 else None
        if candidates is None:
            candidates = set(range(-n + 1, n)) - used
        for a in candidates:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in S}
            if best_survivors is None or len(surv) > len(best_survivors):
                best_a, best_survivors = a, surv
        if best_a is None or not best_survivors:
            return None
        used.add(best_a)
        A.append(best_a)
        U = best_survivors
    if len(U) < k:
        return None
    B = sorted(U)[:k]
    return A, B


def verify_sumset(A: Sequence[int], B: Sequence[int], S: Set[int]) -> bool:
    """Check that every one of the |A|*|B| sums lies in S."""
    return all(a + b in S for a in A for b in B)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Affine cubes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cube_points(u: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> List[int]:
    """All 2^d subset sums u + sum_{i in I} gens[i]."""
    pts = [u]
    for g in gens:
        pts = pts + [p + g for p in pts]
    return pts


def is_proper_cube(u: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff the 2^d subset sums are pairwise distinct."""
    pts = cube_points(u, gens)
    return len(set(pts)) == len(pts)


def greedy_cube(
    S: Set[int], n: int, d: int, proper: bool = True
) -> Optional[Tuple[int, List[int]]]:
    """Greedy affine-cube extraction.

    Invariant: U is a set such that u + x lies in S for every u in U and every subset
    sum x of the generators collected so far.  One round replaces U by
    U intersect (U - a) for the shift a maximising that intersection; if `proper`,
    the shift is additionally forbidden to lie in (cube - cube).
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    gens: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(d):
        cube = cube_points(0, gens)
        forbidden = {x - y for x in cube for y in cube} if proper else {0}
        best_a, best_surv = None, None
        candidates = {v - u for u in U for v in U} - forbidden
        for a in candidates:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in U}
            if best_surv is None or len(surv) > len(best_surv):
                best_a, best_surv = a, surv
        if best_a is None or not best_surv:
            return None
        gens.append(best_a)
        U = best_surv
    if not U:
        return None
    return min(U), gens


def cube_existence_bound(n: int, delta: float, proper: bool = False) -> int:
    """Largest d with (4/delta)^(2^d) [* 4^d] <= 2n, i.e. the guaranteed cube dimension."""
    d = 0
    while True:
        lhs = math.log(4.0 / delta) * (2 ** (d + 1)) + (
            (d + 1) * math.log(4.0) if proper else 0.0
        )
        if lhs > math.log(2.0 * n):
            return d
        d += 1


def cube_avoidance_dimension(n: int, delta: float, eps: float = 0.0) -> int:
    """Least d with (1+eps)(d+1) log n <= 2^d log(1/delta): avoidance becomes possible."""
    d = 1
    while (1 + eps) * (d + 1) * math.log(n) > (2**d) * math.log(1.0 / delta):
        d += 1
        if d > 200:
            raise RuntimeError("no such dimension")
    return d


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. The avoidance (first moment) threshold
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def avoidance_threshold(n: int, delta: float, eps: float = 0.0) -> float:
    """(1 + eps) * log n / log(1/delta): beyond this length, dense progression-free-sumset
    sets exist."""
    return (1 + eps) * math.log(n) / math.log(1.0 / delta)


def naive_first_moment(n: int, delta: float, K: int) -> float:
    """The wasteful union bound  n^3 * delta^(2K-1)  (L-shaped witness, constant 3/2)."""
    return math.exp(3 * math.log(n) + (2 * K - 1) * math.log(delta))


def witness_size(K: int, Q: int) -> int:
    """Number of points a sumset of two K-term progressions is forced to contain.

    With d1 = g e1, d2 = g e2, gcd(e1,e2) = 1 and Q = max(e1,e2), the sumset contains a
    K x min(Q,K) block, and always the (2K-1)-point L-shape.
    """
    return max(2 * K - 1, K * min(Q, K))


def weighted_first_moment(n: int, delta: float, K: int, qmax: int = 200) -> float:
    """The weighted union bound  sum_Q 2 n^2 delta^(witness_size(K,Q))  (constant 1).

    Only O(n^2) parameter triples give a fixed ratio Q, so the sum is geometric; the
    binding term is Q = 1, contributing 2 n^2 delta^(2K-1) and hence the threshold
    K ~ log n / log(1/delta).
    """
    total = 0.0
    for Q in range(1, qmax + 1):
        total += 2 * n * n * delta ** witness_size(K, Q)
    return total

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from itertools import combinations
from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The exact counting criterion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def counting_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Exact criterion of the greedy shift argument.

    Returns True iff  k * window**k <= s_card * (s_card - k)**k,
    where `window` is the size of the admissible shift domain D and `s_card` = |S|.

    Whenever this holds (and k <= min(|S|, |D|)), *every* set S of that size inside
    the corresponding ambient interval/group contains a sumset A + B with
    |A| = |B| = k and A drawn from the shift window.
    """
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return k * window**k <= s_card * (s_card - k) ** k


def _log_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Logarithmic screening version of `counting_criterion` (cheap for huge inputs)."""
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return math.log(k) + k * math.log(window) <= math.log(s_card) + k * math.log(s_card - k)


def max_guaranteed_k(window: int, s_card: int) -> int:
    """Largest k certified by `counting_criterion` (the criterion is monotone in k).

    A logarithmic screening pass locates the crossover cheaply even for astronomically
    large windows; the answer is then confirmed with exact integer arithmetic.
    """
    lo, hi = 0, min(window, s_card)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        if _log_criterion(mid, window, s_card):
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    # exact confirmation in a small neighbourhood of the float crossover
    k = lo
    while k > 0 and not counting_criterion(k, window, s_card):
        k -= 1
    while counting_criterion(k + 1, window, s_card):
        k += 1
    return k


def interval_guarantee(n: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Guaranteed sumset size for a delta-dense subset of [0, n), naive window D = (-n, n)."""
    return max_guaranteed_k(2 * n, math.ceil(delta * n))


def group_guarantee(order: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Guaranteed sumset size for a delta-dense subset of an abelian group of given order."""
    return max_guaranteed_k(order, math.ceil(delta * order))


def asymptotic_prediction(n: int, delta: float) -> float:
    """The theoretical value log n / log(1/delta)."""
    return math.log(n) / math.log(1.0 / delta)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Constructive greedy shift extraction of a sumset
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def greedy_sumset(
    S: Set[int], n: int, k: int
) -> Optional[Tuple[List[int], List[int]]]:
    """Greedy shift algorithm.

    Repeatedly pick the unused shift a in (-n, n) maximising |{u in U : u + a in S}|,
    and replace U by that surviving set.  After k rounds, if |U| >= k, the collected
    shifts A and any k-subset B of U satisfy A + B subset of S.

    Returns (A, B) or None if the greedy run does not reach size k.
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    A: List[int] = []
    used: Set[int] = set()
    for _ in range(k):
        best_a, best_survivors = None, None
        # candidate shifts: differences of S are the only ones that can help
        candidates = {s - u for s in S for u in U} - used if len(U) < 200 else None
        if candidates is None:
            candidates = set(range(-n + 1, n)) - used
        for a in candidates:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in S}
            if best_survivors is None or len(surv) > len(best_survivors):
                best_a, best_survivors = a, surv
        if best_a is None or not best_survivors:
            return None
        used.add(best_a)
        A.append(best_a)
        U = best_survivors
    if len(U) < k:
        return None
    B = sorted(U)[:k]
    return A, B


def verify_sumset(A: Sequence[int], B: Sequence[int], S: Set[int]) -> bool:
    """Check that every one of the |A|*|B| sums lies in S."""
    return all(a + b in S for a in A for b in B)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Affine cubes
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cube_points(u: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> List[int]:
    """All 2^d subset sums u + sum_{i in I} gens[i]."""
    pts = [u]
    for g in gens:
        pts = pts + [p + g for p in pts]
    return pts


def is_proper_cube(u: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff the 2^d subset sums are pairwise distinct."""
    pts = cube_points(u, gens)
    return len(set(pts)) == len(pts)


def greedy_cube(
    S: Set[int], n: int, d: int, proper: bool = True
) -> Optional[Tuple[int, List[int]]]:
    """Greedy affine-cube extraction.

    Invariant: U is a set such that u + x lies in S for every u in U and every subset
    sum x of the generators collected so far.  One round replaces U by
    U intersect (U - a) for the shift a maximising that intersection; if `proper`,
    the shift is additionally forbidden to lie in (cube - cube).
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    gens: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(d):
        cube = cube_points(0, gens)
        forbidden = {x - y for x in cube for y in cube} if proper else {0}
        best_a, best_surv = None, None
        candidates = {v - u for u in U for v in U} - forbidden
        for a in candidates:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in U}
            if best_surv is None or len(surv) > len(best_surv):
                best_a, best_surv = a, surv
        if best_a is None or not best_surv:
            return None
        gens.append(best_a)
        U = best_surv
    if not U:
        return None
    return min(U), gens


def cube_existence_bound(n: int, delta: float, proper: bool = False) -> int:
    """Largest d with (4/delta)^(2^d) [* 4^d] <= 2n, i.e. the guaranteed cube dimension."""
    d = 0
    while True:
        lhs = math.log(4.0 / delta) * (2 ** (d + 1)) + (
            (d + 1) * math.log(4.0) if proper else 0.0
        )
        if lhs > math.log(2.0 * n):
            return d
        d += 1


def cube_avoidance_dimension(n: int, delta: float, eps: float = 0.0) -> int:
    """Least d with (1+eps)(d+1) log n <= 2^d log(1/delta): avoidance becomes possible."""
    d = 1
    while (1 + eps) * (d + 1) * math.log(n) > (2**d) * math.log(1.0 / delta):
        d += 1
        if d > 200:
            raise RuntimeError("no such dimension")
    return d


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. The avoidance (first moment) threshold
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def avoidance_threshold(n: int, delta: float, eps: float = 0.0) -> float:
    """(1 + eps) * log n / log(1/delta): beyond this length, dense progression-free-sumset
    sets exist."""
    return (1 + eps) * math.log(n) / math.log(1.0 / delta)


def naive_first_moment(n: int, delta: float, K: int) -> float:
    """The wasteful union bound  n^3 * delta^(2K-1)  (L-shaped witness, constant 3/2)."""
    return math.exp(3 * math.log(n) + (2 * K - 1) * math.log(delta))


def witness_size(K: int, Q: int) -> int:
    """Number of points a sumset of two K-term progressions is forced to contain.

    With d1 = g e1, d2 = g e2, gcd(e1,e2) = 1 and Q = max(e1,e2), the sumset contains a
    K x min(Q,K) block, and always the (2K-1)-point L-shape.
    """
    return max(2 * K - 1, K * min(Q, K))


def weighted_first_moment(n: int, delta: float, K: int, qmax: int = 200) -> float:
    """The weighted union bound  sum_Q 2 n^2 delta^(witness_size(K,Q))  (constant 1).

    Only O(n^2) parameter triples give a fixed ratio Q, so the sum is geometric; the
    binding term is Q = 1, contributing 2 n^2 delta^(2K-1) and hence the threshold
    K ~ log n / log(1/delta).
    """
    total = 0.0
    for Q in range(1, qmax + 1):
        total += 2 * n * n * delta ** witness_size(K, Q)
    return total

def has_sumset(S: Set[int], k: int) -> bool:

    return False

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple


def greedy_shift_sumset(
    S: Set[int], k: int, shift_window: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None
) -> Optional[Tuple[List[int], List[int]]]:
    """Extract A, B with |A| = |B| = k and A + B subset of S.

    The algorithm maintains a survivor set U with the invariant

        u + a  in S    for every u in U and every shift a collected so far.

    At each round it picks the unused shift a maximising |{u in U : u + a in S}|.  The
    averaging identity  sum_{a in D} |{u in U : u + a in S}| = |U| |S|  guarantees that the
    maximum is at least |U|(|S| - #used)/|D|, so after k rounds

        |U| >= |S| ((|S| - k)/|D|)^k,

    and the run succeeds whenever k|D|^k <= |S|(|S| - k)^k.

    Complexity: O(k * |D| * |U|) membership tests; the survivor set shrinks geometrically,
    so the first round dominates in practice.  Returns None if the run cannot reach size k.
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    A: List[int] = []
    used: Set[int] = set()
    D: Set[int] = set(shift_window) if shift_window is not None else {s - u for s in S for u in S}

    for _ in range(k):
        best_a: Optional[int] = None
        best_surv: Optional[Set[int]] = None
        for a in D - used:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in S}
            if best_surv is None or len(surv) > len(best_surv):
                best_a, best_surv = a, surv
        if best_a is None or best_surv is None or not best_surv:
            return None
        used.add(best_a)
        A.append(best_a)
        U = best_surv

    if len(U) < k:
        return None
    return A, sorted(U)[:k]


def verify_sumset(A: Sequence[int], B: Sequence[int], S: Set[int]) -> bool:
    """Confirm that all |A|*|B| sums lie in S."""
    return all(a + b in S for a in A for b in B)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple


def cube_points(base: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> List[int]:
    """All 2^d subset sums base + sum_{i in I} gens[i]."""
    pts = [base]
    for g in gens:
        pts = pts + [p + g for p in pts]
    return pts


def greedy_proper_cube(
    S: Set[int], d: int
) -> Optional[Tuple[int, List[int]]]:
    """Extract a proper affine cube of dimension d inside S.

    Invariant: U is a set such that u + x lies in S for every u in U and every subset sum x
    of the generators found so far.  One round replaces U by U ∩ (U - a), which is exactly
    the statement that the cube may be extended by the generator a.  Because each round
    intersects U with a translate of itself, the density is squared at every step:
    |U_{j+1}| >~ |U_j|^2/|D|, so after d rounds the density is about delta^(2^d) and the
    process runs for d ≈ log2(log n / log(1/delta)) rounds.

    Properness is enforced by forbidding the new generator to lie in the difference set
    (C - C) of the cube built so far, a set of at most 4^j elements; a generator outside it
    is automatically nonzero and doubles the number of distinct cube points.

    Complexity: O(d * |U|^2) difference candidates, each tested in O(|U|).
    """
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    gens: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(d):
        cube = cube_points(0, gens)
        forbidden = {x - y for x in cube for y in cube}
        best_a: Optional[int] = None
        best_surv: Optional[Set[int]] = None
        for a in {v - u for u in U for v in U} - forbidden:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in U}
            if best_surv is None or len(surv) > len(best_surv):
                best_a, best_surv = a, surv
        if best_a is None or best_surv is None or not best_surv:
            return None
        gens.append(best_a)
        U = best_surv
    if not U:
        return None
    return min(U), gens


def is_proper(base: int, gens: Sequence[int]) -> bool:
    """True iff the 2^d subset sums are pairwise distinct."""
    pts = cube_points(base, gens)
    return len(set(pts)) == len(pts)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Tuple


def counting_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Exact existence criterion k * window^k <= s_card * (s_card - k)^k (exact integers)."""
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return k * window**k <= s_card * (s_card - k) ** k


def _log_criterion(k: int, window: int, s_card: int) -> bool:
    """Logarithmic screening of the same criterion (cheap for astronomically large input)."""
    if k <= 0:
        return True
    if k > s_card or k > window:
        return False
    return math.log(k) + k * math.log(window) <= math.log(s_card) + k * math.log(s_card - k)


def certified_grid_size(n: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Largest k such that EVERY delta-dense subset of [n] provably contains a k x k grid.

    Binary search on the monotone logarithmic criterion, then exact integer confirmation.
    Complexity: O(log n) logarithmic evaluations plus O(1) exact big-integer powers.
    """
    m = math.ceil(delta * n)
    lo, hi = 0, min(2 * n, m)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi + 1) // 2
        if _log_criterion(mid, 2 * n, m):
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    k = lo
    while k > 0 and not counting_criterion(k, 2 * n, m):
        k -= 1
    while counting_criterion(k + 1, 2 * n, m):
        k += 1
    return k


def witness_size(K: int, Q: int) -> int:
    """Points forced by a sumset of two K-term progressions with reduced ratio Q."""
    return max(2 * K - 1, K * min(Q, K))


def weighted_first_moment(n: int, delta: float, K: int, qmax: int = 200) -> float:
    """Weighted union bound  sum_Q 2 n^2 x^{witness_size(K,Q)}  with x = delta + 1/n."""
    x = delta + 1.0 / n
    total = 0.0
    for Q in range(1, qmax + 1):
        total += 2 * n * n * x ** witness_size(K, Q)
    return total


def avoidance_certificate(n: int, delta: float) -> int:
    """Least K for which a delta-dense subset of [n] avoiding all such sumsets is certified.

    Monotone in K, so a simple upward scan suffices; the value is
    (1 + o(1)) log n / log(1/delta).
    """
    K = 2
    while weighted_first_moment(n, delta, K) >= 1.0:
        K += 1
        if K > 10000:
            raise RuntimeError("no certificate found")
    return K


def threshold_window(n: int, delta: float) -> Tuple[int, int, float]:
    """(certified existence size, certified avoidance size, the scale log n / log(1/delta))."""
    return (
        certified_grid_size(n, delta),
        avoidance_certificate(n, delta),
        math.log(n) / math.log(1.0 / delta),
    )

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


def greedy_sumset(S: Set[int], k: int) -> Tuple[List[int], List[int], List[int]]:
    """Greedy shift extraction; returns (shifts, survivor set, sizes after each step)."""
    U: Set[int] = set(S)
    shifts: List[int] = []
    sizes: List[int] = [len(U)]
    used: Set[int] = set()
    for _ in range(k):
        cand = {s - u for s in S for u in U} - used
        best_a, best_surv = None, None
        for a in cand:
            surv = {u for u in U if u + a in S}
            if best_surv is None or len(surv) > len(best_surv):
                best_a, best_surv = a, surv
        if best_a is None or not best_surv:
            break
        used.add(best_a)
        shifts.append(best_a)
        U = best_surv
        sizes.append(len(U))
    return shifts, sorted(U), sizes


def main() -> None:
    random.seed(7)
    n, delta, k = 300, 0.5, 4
    m = int(delta * n)
    S = set(random.sample(range(n), m))
    shifts, U, sizes = greedy_sumset(S, k)
    B = U[: len(shifts)]
    grid = [[a + b for b in B] for a in shifts]

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(13, 7))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, height_ratios=[1.15, 1])

    # Panel 1: the set and the grid
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
    per_row = 60
    rows = math.ceil(n / per_row)
    img = np.zeros((rows, per_row))
    grid_pts = {v for row in grid for v in row}
    for x in range(n):
        r, c = divmod(x, per_row)
        img[r, c] = 3 if x in grid_pts else (2 if x in S else 1)
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="Blues", vmin=0, vmax=3, aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest")
    ax.set_title(f"S ⊆ [{n}) with |S| = {m} (mid tone), and the extracted grid A+B (dark)")
    ax.set_xlabel("value mod 60")
    ax.set_ylabel("value ÷ 60")

    # Panel 2: decay of the survivor set
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
    steps = list(range(len(sizes)))
    ax.semilogy(steps, sizes, "o-", color="#1f77b4", label="observed |U| after each step")
    guarantee = [max(1.0, m * ((m - k) / (2.0 * n)) ** j) for j in steps]
    ax.semilogy(steps, guarantee, "s--", color="#d62728",
                label=r"guarantee $|S|\,((|S|-k)/|D|)^j$")
    ax.set_xlabel("greedy step $j$")
    ax.set_ylabel("survivors")
    ax.set_title("Geometric decay of the survivor set")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")

    # Panel 3: the grid of sums
    ax = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
    arr = np.array([[1 if v in S else 0 for v in row] for row in grid])
    ax.imshow(arr, cmap="Greens", vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="nearest")
    for i, row in enumerate(grid):
        for j, v in enumerate(row):
            ax.text(j, i, str(v), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(B)), [str(b) for b in B])
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(shifts)), [str(a) for a in shifts])
    ax.set_xlabel("B")
    ax.set_ylabel("A")
    ax.set_title(f"All {len(shifts)}×{len(B)} sums a+b lie in S")

    fig.suptitle("The greedy shift process: from a dense set to a perfect additive grid",
                 fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("greedy_process.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote greedy_process.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<script>
(function(){

  let S = new Set(), U = [], shifts = [], gens = [], found = new Set(), mode = "sum", done=false;

  const structNames = ["random","intervals","residues"];

  function buildS(){
    S = new Set();
    const m = Math.ceil(delta*n);
    if(structure===0){
      const pool = [...Array(n).keys()];
      for(let i=pool.length-1;i>0;i--){const j=(Math.random()*(i+1))|0;[pool[i],pool[j]]=[pool[j],pool[i]];}
      pool.slice(0,m).forEach(x=>S.add(x));
    } else if(structure===1){
      const block = Math.max(2, Math.round(n/24));
      let count=0, guard=0;
      while(count<m && guard++<10000){
        const st=(Math.random()*(n-block))|0;
        for(let x=st;x<st+block && count<m;x++){ if(!S.has(x)){S.add(x);count++;} }
      }
    } else {
      const mm = Math.max(3, Math.round(1/delta)+1);
      const keep = Math.max(1, Math.round(delta*mm));
      for(let x=0;x<n;x++) if((x%mm)<keep) S.add(x);
      let x=0; while(S.size<m && x<n){ if(!S.has(x)) S.add(x); x++; }
    }
    resetProcess();
  }

  function resetProcess(){
    U = [...S].sort((a,b)=>a-b);
    shifts=[]; gens=[]; found=new Set(); done=false;
    log("<span class='dim'>new run — |S| = "+S.size+", density "+(S.size/n).toFixed(3)+"</span>");
    draw(); stats();
  }

  function log(msg){
    const L=$("log"); L.innerHTML += msg+"<br/>"; L.scrollTop = L.scrollHeight;
  }

  function cubePoints(gs){
    let pts=[0];
    for(const g of gs){ pts = pts.concat(pts.map(p=>p+g)); }
    return pts;
  }

  function stepSum(){
    if(done) return;
    const used = new Set(shifts);
    let bestA=null, bestSurv=null;
    const cand = new Set();
    for(const s of S) for(const u of U){ const a=s-u; if(!used.has(a)) cand.add(a); }
    for(const a of cand){
      let surv=[]; for(const u of U) if(S.has(u+a)) surv.push(u);
      if(bestSurv===null || surv.length>bestSurv.length){ bestA=a; bestSurv=surv; }
    }
    if(bestA===null || bestSurv.length===0){ done=true; log("<span class='no'>no useful shift remains — process stops</span>"); return; }
    shifts.push(bestA); U=bestSurv;
    log("shift a<sub>"+shifts.length+"</sub> = <b>"+bestA+"</b>   survivors |U| = "+U.length
        +" <span class='dim'>(ratio "+(U.length/Math.max(1,S.size)).toFixed(3)+" of |S|)</span>");
    if(U.length < shifts.length){ done=true; log("<span class='dim'>survivor set smaller than the number of shifts — stopping</span>"); }
    markFound(); draw(); stats();
  }

  function stepCube(){
    if(done) return;
    const cube = cubePoints(gens);
    const forb = new Set();
    for(const x of cube) for(const y of cube) forb.add(x-y);
    let bestA=null,bestSurv=null;
    const Uset = new Set(U);
    const cand = new Set();
    for(const u of U) for(const v of U){ const a=v-u; if(a!==0 && !forb.has(a)) cand.add(a); }
    for(const a of cand){
      let surv=[]; for(const u of U) if(Uset.has(u+a)) surv.push(u);
      if(bestSurv===null || surv.length>bestSurv.length){ bestA=a; bestSurv=surv; }
    }
    if(bestA===null || bestSurv.length===0){ done=true; log("<span class='no'>cannot extend the cube any further</span>"); return; }
    gens.push(bestA); U=bestSurv;
    log("generator a<sub>"+gens.length+"</sub> = <b>"+bestA+"</b>   survivors |U| = "+U.length
        +" <span class='dim'>(dimension "+gens.length+", 2^"+gens.length+" = "+(1<<gens.length)+" points)</span>");
    markFound(); draw(); stats();
  }

  function markFound(){
    found = new Set();
    if(mode==="sum"){
      if(U.length===0) return;
      const k = shifts.length;
      const B = U.slice(0, Math.max(1,Math.min(k,U.length)));
      for(const a of shifts) for(const b of B) found.add(a+b);
      for(const b of B) found.add(b);
    } else {
      if(U.length===0) return;
      const u = U[0];
      for(const x of cubePoints(gens)) found.add(u+x);
    }
  }

  function verify(){
    if(mode==="sum"){
      const k=shifts.length; if(k===0||U.length<1) return null;
      const B=U.slice(0,Math.min(k,U.length));
      let ok=true; for(const a of shifts) for(const b of B) if(!S.has(a+b)) ok=false;
      return {ok:ok, txt:(ok?"✓ ":"✗ ")+k+"×"+B.length};
    } else {
      if(U.length===0 || gens.length===0) return null;
      const u=U[0], pts=cubePoints(gens).map(x=>u+x);
      const ok = pts.every(p=>S.has(p)) && (new Set(pts)).size===pts.length;
      return {ok:ok, txt:(ok?"✓ ":"✗ ")+"dim "+gens.length+", "+pts.length+" pts"};
    }
  }

  function certifiedK(){
    const m=S.size; let best=0;
    for(let k=1;k<=Math.min(m-1,60);k++){
      const lhs = Math.log(k)+k*Math.log(2*n);
      const rhs = Math.log(m)+k*Math.log(m-k);
      if(lhs<=rhs) best=k; else break;
    }
    return best;
  }

  function draw(){
    const W=cv.width, H=cv.height;
    ctx.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
    const cols = Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(n*W/H));
    const cell = Math.max(6, Math.min(Math.floor(W/cols), 26));
    const perRow = Math.floor(W/cell);
    const Uset=new Set(U);
    for(let x=0;x<n;x++){
      const r=Math.floor(x/perRow), c=x%perRow;
      const px=c*cell+1, py=r*cell+1, sz=cell-2;
      let col="#22305c";
      if(S.has(x)) col="#6ee7ff";
      if(Uset.has(x)) col="#ffd166";
      if(found.has(x)) col="#7ef2a5";
      ctx.fillStyle=col;
      ctx.fillRect(px,py,sz,sz);
    }
  }

  function stats(){
    $("sS").textContent = S.size;
    $("sU").textContent = U.length;
    $("sK").textContent = (mode==="sum"? shifts.length : gens.length);
    $("sC").textContent = certifiedK();
    $("sL").textContent = (Math.log(n)/Math.log(1/delta)).toFixed(2);
    const v = verify();
    $("sV").innerHTML = v? (v.ok? "<span class='ok'>"+v.txt+"</span>" : "<span class='no'>"+v.txt+"</span>") : "—";
  }

  $("n").oninput = e=>{ n=+e.target.value; $("nv").textContent=n; buildS(); };
  $("d").oninput = e=>{ delta=(+e.target.value)/100; $("dv").textContent=delta.toFixed(2); buildS(); };
  $("s").oninput = e=>{ structure=+e.target.value; $("sv").textContent=structNames[structure]; buildS(); };
  $("gen").onclick = buildS;
  $("reset").onclick = resetProcess;
  $("step").onclick = ()=> mode==="sum"? stepSum() : stepCube();
  $("run").onclick = ()=>{ let guard=0; while(!done && guard++<40){ mode==="sum"? stepSum():stepCube(); } };
  $("mSum").onclick = ()=>{ mode="sum"; $("mSum").classList.add("on"); $("mCube").classList.remove("on"); resetProcess(); };
  $("mCube").onclick = ()=>{ mode="cube"; $("mCube").classList.add("on"); $("mSum").classList.remove("on"); resetProcess(); };

  buildS();
})();
</script>
